**Short answer: 30W is the minimum, and 65-70W is the sweet spot if you want faster charging.** The right figure depends on your model.

**What Apple recommends** ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)):
- **2022 or later:** 30W (13-inch only), 35W dual-port, 67W, or 70W.
- **2018-2021:** 30W, or the 40W Dynamic adapter (60W max).
- **Fast charging:** Apple lists 70W or higher USB PD for the current M5 models ([Apple specs](https://www.apple.com/macbook-air/specs/?subId1=UUtbUdUnU72396YYw&subId2=dtb)). The M4 13-inch lists the 70W adapter ([M4 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).

**What's in the box:**
- **M5 13-inch:** a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ([M5 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **M4 13-inch:** 30W with the 8-core GPU, or 35W dual-port with the 10-core GPU.

Any USB-C power adapter that supports USB Power Delivery will charge a USB-C-charging Mac, even at higher or lower wattage than Apple recommends. For the best experience, Apple suggests at least the wattage of the adapter it recommends for your model.

**If you want a spare or travel charger:** The [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) is $49.99. It gives 65W from a single USB-C port. With several devices plugged in, the main USB-C port holds 45W, which still charges a MacBook Air. Keep the laptop on that port. Because it tops out at 65W, it won't hit Apple's 70W fast-charge level. That's a Dealectric affiliate link, so they're paid if you buy, at no cost to you. Their source says it doesn't include Apple's official wattage figures, so I used Apple's pages for those.

I didn't get a direct store link for Apple's own adapters. If you want the 70W fast-charge option, it's listed on Apple's MacBook Air configuration page.

If you tell me your model and year, I can narrow this down.
